extracted.intended_audience: grant reviewers and molecular microbiology/chemical biology researchers (authors and peers preparing/examining an NIH-style research strategy)
extracted.subtask_description: Crafting or evaluating an NIH-style Research Strategy describing specific aims, hypotheses, and experimental approaches for biochemical, genetic, structural, and biophysical studies of the S. aureus agr quorum-sensing system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, testable Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: State explicit aims that break the project into focused, answerable questions (e.g., 'Aim 1. To determine the mechanisms of AIP biosynthesis and secretion.' 'AIM 2. To understand the mechanism of activation and inhibition of the agr two component system.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each aim should include sub-questions/sub-aims (e.g., 1.1, 1.2, 1.3) that define specific mechanistic issues to be resolved and outline the experimental logic for how the aim will be addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis-driven experiments with explicit predictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate mechanistic hypotheses and state expected experimental outcomes (e.g., 'We hypothesize that ClpP complex is directly responsible for degradation of AgrDC' with prediction 'increase in AgrD and AgrDC levels, but a decrease in the amount of AIP').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, testable predictions that allow interpretation of results; use these predictions to design decisive assays (e.g., genetic mutation should alter measurable protein/peptide levels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use both candidate-based and unbiased approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine hypothesis-driven (candidate) tests with discovery (unbiased) methods when identifying enzymes/transporters (e.g., test ClpP and also perform activity-guided fractionation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe parallel strategies so negative results in candidate approaches are complemented by unbiased screens; specify assays for each path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthogonal/Complementary methods for validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ multiple independent assay types (immunoblotting, mass spectrometry, bioassays, RP-HPLC, FRET, structural methods) to validate findings (e.g., measure AgrD/AgrDC by immunoblotting, AIP by MS and bioassays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use orthogonal readouts to strengthen conclusions and rule out assay-specific artifacts; list the techniques and what each will report.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vitro and in vivo validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify biochemical activities using purified/recombinant systems and confirm physiological relevance via genetic deletions or cellular assays (e.g., in vitro proteolysis and in vivo genetic deletions in S. aureus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan experiments that demonstrate mechanism both in controlled biochemical systems and in the native cellular context; include the genetic tools and phenotypic readouts to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development and use of tailored biochemical probes/assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Design specific reagents and assays (e.g., AgrDC substrate peptide with fluorescein-dabsyl FRET pair, intein-fusion strategy, diazirine photocrosslinkers, biotinylated AIP analogs, non-hydrolysable isosteres) to detect, enrich, or trap activities and interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail probe chemistry, assay design, and expected signal change on reaction; include controls and downstream identification methods (e.g., MS analysis of enriched fractions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate internal controls and assay integrity checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Include internal standards and controls in assays (e.g., poly-Glu charged peptide as control in liposome partitioning assays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define negative/positive controls and internal recovery standards to ensure assays are working and to interpret negative results reliably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity-guided fractionation and proteomic identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multi-step biochemical fractionation guided by activity readouts (fluorescence reporter, bioassay, MS) followed by mass spectrometry to identify proteins in active fractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the activity assay for fractionation, criteria for selecting active fractions, and downstream methods for protein identification and recombinant candidate testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affinity-enrichment and crosslinking to trap enzyme–substrate complexes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use substrate analogs with non-hydrolysable isosteres or photocrosslinkers to trap enzyme–substrate complexes for MS-based identification (e.g., hydroxyethylene, phosphinates, reduced amides, photo-leucine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe placement of isosteres/crosslinkers, enrichment handles (biotin), and MS workflows; plan biochemical and genetic validation of identified enzymes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence-function mapping via mutagenesis/scanning
rubrics_metrics.description: Map substrate recognition and cleavage sites by systematic mutational analysis (e.g., alanine-scan of AgrDC, length extensions, chimera swaps to define linker-determined cleavage sites).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both biochemical assays of proteolysis and in vivo expression of mutants to test effects on processing and functional readouts (AIP production, bioassays).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of feasibility via preliminary data and availability of tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite preliminary experiments, available reagents/tools, and prior success to support feasibility (e.g., tools already available in lab, prior reconstitution data, preliminary crosslinking and liposome processing results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state which required materials/assays are in hand and how preliminary results inform experimental design and expected outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative/thermodynamic reasoning and numerical estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Use quantitative estimates and thermodynamic/kinetic arguments to motivate experiments (e.g., AIP concentration reaches 5 µM, estimate AgrDC half-life ~10 s, equilibrium constants suggest need for rapid degradation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include simple calculations or parameter estimates that reveal mechanistic constraints and justify the proposed experimental focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation of alternative explanations and contingency plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss plausible alternative mechanisms and outline experiments or alternative strategies if initial hypotheses fail (e.g., if AgrB not involved in transport test passive diffusion and alternate transporters; if SpsB is inefficient, search for additional proteases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each key hypothesis, present at least one alternative and a clear plan to discriminate between them; ensure experimental paths are adaptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of structural and biophysical approaches to link mechanism to dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine crystallography, nanodisc systems, single-molecule FRET, and other biophysical tools to relate ligand binding and conformational changes to receptor activity (e.g., GCN4-AgrC chimeras, TIRF single-molecule FRET).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe construct design strategies, labeling plans, expected FRET behaviors for activity states, and how structural snapshots and dynamics together will test the mechanistic model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of model constructs to trap distinct activity states
rubrics_metrics.description: Engineer chimeric/model proteins (e.g., GCN4-AgrC fusions) to stabilize 'off', 'basal', and 'on' states for structural and functional analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how construct series will be designed and used to obtain a structural series; include validation that constructs reproduce relevant biochemical activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-resolution mapping combining ligand- and receptor-based crosslinking
rubrics_metrics.description: Use complementary crosslinking strategies from both the ligand (biotinylated AIP analogs with diazirine/benzophenone) and the receptor (site-specifically installed benzoylphenylalanine via amber suppression) to pinpoint binding site residues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage both sides to get residue-level resolution, use enrichment handles for MS and/or direct readouts from genetically encoded crosslinkers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for technical challenges and optimization strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge likely technical hurdles (e.g., crystallization of dynamic complexes, small membrane sensor domains below cryo-EM size threshold) and provide concrete remediation plans (screen homologs, optimize constructs, use specialized membrane-protein crystallization screens).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List anticipated problems and the sequential steps/resources that will be used to overcome them, demonstrating realistic project management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborations and access to specialized expertise/instrumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and leverage collaborators with specialized skills/infrastructure (e.g., single-molecule biophysics collaborator with TIRF instrumentation) to perform experiments beyond the core lab's capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the collaborator, their contributions, and how their expertise/instrumentation enables critical experiments, including letters of support when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of quantitative, activity-based readouts to drive purification and screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Rely on measurable activity signals (bioassays, fluorescence generation, RP-HPLC) to guide fractionation, screening, and selection of candidates for further study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the sensitivity and expected dynamic range of activity assays and how positive/negative thresholds will be used during fractionation and candidate triage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional phenotypic assays to demonstrate biological relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use cell-based bioassays and MS of culture supernatants to show that biochemical manipulations impact physiological AIP production and agr signaling (e.g., bioassays to detect AIP production in ⊗pmt strain, mass spectrometry analysis of supernatants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that biochemical findings are correlated with measurable phenotypes in cells or culture supernatants to establish relevance to virulence regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic SAR (structure–activity relationship) to guide mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform systematic SAR analysis (e.g., chimeras, residue changes converting agonists to antagonists) to define how small sequence/length changes affect function and to infer enzymatic specificity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SAR data to prioritize candidate proteases/processing models and to design selective probes or inhibitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit readouts for discrimination of substrate specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Design experiments to test how proteolytic machinery discriminates between related substrates (e.g., full-length AgrD vs AgrDC via localization or peptide length alterations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose assays that alter localization (membrane-anchoring amphipathic helices) or peptide length and measure susceptibility to degradation both in vitro and in vivo.
